nodes.label: Per-user teams
nodes.rationale: Per-user bots with private rooms so one user's finances never leak into another's chat; bots have no schedule and only run on messages.

nodes.label: Self-hosted model (LLM_*)
nodes.rationale: Used for anything touching user data: per-user teams, merchant screening, bank-email parsing.

nodes.label: Third-party desk LLM (DESK_LLM_*)
nodes.rationale: Optional third-party OpenAI-compatible model for shared desks only, because they handle public data; falls back to the self-hosted model when unset.

nodes.label: Data boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Only shared desks may use the third-party model; their tools read public data with no user IDs; merchant names derived from user activity are screened first.

nodes.label: Automatic deal use detection
nodes.rationale: No LLM is involved; transactions from bank alerts are matched against offered deals by merchant, date window, card and minimum spend.

nodes.label: avail_deal already_counted
nodes.rationale: Prevents the same purchase saving twice when the user later reports a deal that was already auto-detected.

nodes.label: Merchant screening (business vs private payee)
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted model classifies merchants so private payees (personal) never reach third-party desk bots; business merchants become pending.

nodes.label: Per-user bots instead of shared ones
nodes.rationale: OMB copies a bot's recent activity from other chats into every prompt, so a shared bot would leak one user's finances into another's chat.
nodes.norm_label: per-user bots instead of shared ones

nodes.label: Member key in room bulletin
nodes.rationale: OMB allows at most 20 tool servers per workspace, so two are used and each user's bots pass a per-room key on every tool call.

nodes.label: Per-bot tool allow-lists (32 tools)
nodes.rationale: OMB's default of 72 tools (~22k tokens) was trimmed to 32 for user bots.

nodes.label: Gmail direct Google OAuth
nodes.rationale: OMB's connector is workspace-shared and capped at 5 accounts.

nodes.label: offer_deal rule
nodes.rationale: Every recommended deal must be offered via offer_deal so the app can detect later use from bank alerts.

nodes.label: Automatic deal detection (do not ask if used)
nodes.norm_label: automatic deal detection (do not ask if used)

nodes.label: Never invent deals rule
nodes.rationale: Deals change; availability must come from tools, not memory.

nodes.label: No card digits/CVV/PIN/OTP rule
nodes.rationale: Only the card type matters; sensitive data must never be requested.

nodes.label: Deal confidence scoring (0.9/0.6/<0.5)
nodes.rationale: Explicit official terms get 0.9, social posts 0.6, unsure below 0.5 which routes to admin review.

nodes.label: Only save what was seen rule
nodes.rationale: Never invent amounts, dates or card requirements; the page always wins over catalog wording.
nodes.norm_label: only save what was seen rule

nodes.label: Team roster (Savings Coach, Deals Advisor, Investment Advisor)
nodes.norm_label: team roster (savings coach, deals advisor, investment advisor)

nodes.label: No card digits/CVV/PIN/OTP rule
nodes.rationale: Only the card type is saved; if shared, the person is told not to share it and it is not stored.

nodes.label: Style rules (language mirroring, Islamic finance aware)
nodes.norm_label: style rules (language mirroring, islamic finance aware)

nodes.label: DESK_LLM_* env vars
nodes.rationale: Empty means shared desks fall back to LLM_*.

nodes.label: app_user non-superuser role
nodes.rationale: The app connects as a non-superuser so Postgres row level security applies; migrations use the superuser URL.

nodes.label: Worker exactly 1 replica
nodes.rationale: A single scheduler avoids duplicate scheduled jobs.
